### Frame Material Specifications

**Material:** 
Duracast® fiberglass composite - Pella's five-layer fiberglass, the strongest material available for windows and patio doors, engineered for lasting durability


**Thermal Properties:** 
Our fiberglass has virtually the same expansion and contraction as the glass, almost none. This helps reduce the risk for air-seal failure and provides long-term stability for dependable operation


**Construction Quality:** 
Secured with corner locks, metal fasteners and injected with sealant for added strength, durability and reliable water performance


**Temperature Resistance:** 
Tested from -40ºF to 180ºF. Withstands high heat and subzero cold. Duracast fiberglass composite resists warping in summer and becoming brittle during winter


### Hardware and Security Features

**Locking System:** 
Exclusive cam-action lock design improves the security of the window and creates a stronger seal by reaching out and grabbing the opposing sash and pulling it into the other sash


**Operation:** 
Sashes tilt in, allowing you to easily clean the exterior of your windows from inside your home


### Finish and Color Options

**Powder-Coat Finish:** 
The durable powder-coat finish resists chalking, fading and scratching


**Color Options:** 
Pella Impervia fiberglass products have a long-lasting factory powder-coat finish in your choice of five colors. Dual-color frames have White on the interior with Brown, Tan, Morning Sky Gray or Black on the exterior

## 4. RED FINDINGS / SAFETY CONCERNS

### Active CPSC Recalls - Product Not Affected

**Casement Window Recall (2024):** 
Pella Recalls Casement Windows Due to Injury Hazard. Consumers should keep the recalled casement windows shut and locked at all times and contact Pella to receive a free repair by a Pella-designated service technician
 - Does NOT affect Impervia double-hung series

**Battery Ingestion Recall (2025):** 
Pella Recalls Sliding Patio Doors and Windows Due to Battery Ingestion Hazard. Affects Pella Reserve and Lifestyle Sliding Patio Doors and Lifestyle Windows with motorized features sold from March 2024 through June 2024
 - Does NOT affect standard Impervia DH

## 5. YELLOW FLAGS / AMBIGUITIES

### Industry Expert Critical Assessment

**Air Infiltration Concerns:** 
Industry insiders cite air infiltration rate of 0.18 – not very impressive (compare with an Okna 800 window with an air infiltration rate of 0.01)

The Impervia lacks the overall strength and durability when compared to other fiberglass options such as the Milgard Ultra window. However, for the same price there are better options for the consumer that will offer better long term value and performance

## 7. FIELD SOURCE OPINIONS

### Mixed Professional Sentiment

**Installation Quality Concerns:** 
Professional installers reported frame bowing and plastic flange issues requiring extensive shimming
 [INSTALL-CONFOUND: MEDIUM]

**Consumer Experience - Positive:** 
We had our new Pella Impervia's installed on this past Friday and I am very impressed with the Windows. The open very easily, the installers did a great job with the install


**Consumer Experience - Mixed:** 
I swapped out my old windows for Impervia about two winters ago. Honestly, they've been pretty great at keeping the chill out—my heating bills actually dropped noticeably. Fiberglass frames seem to handle temperature swings really well without warping


**Professional Builder Assessment:** 
I've installed quite a few of both Lifestyle and Impervia windows. Impervia, on the other hand, is pretty much set-and-forget thanks to fiberglass durability. I've seen them hold up impressively well in some brutal weather (think Wisconsin winters, ice storms, and all that fun stuff...)


**Critical Professional Opinion:** 
For a premium window, I didn't like what appeared to be PVC beads on the outside on the display model. Also, the Impervia's thermal performance is average at best. I stayed away from Pella as I had heard terrible stories about their customer service


**Field Consensus:** Mixed sentiment with positive durability feedback balanced against installation challenges and customer service concerns. Some professionals prefer alternatives (Marvin Essential, Alpen).
